2 ريّم عَلَيْهِ , (T, K,) inf. n. تَرْيِيمٌ, (TA,) He exceeded him; (T, K, TA;) i. e., one man, another; (T;) in journeying, or pace, and the like: from رَيْمٌ as signifying زِيَادَةٌ and فَضْلٌ [i. e. “ excess, ” &c.], or as signifying بَرَاحٌ [expl. above]. (TA.) ―
-b2- ريّم بِالمَكَانِ, (ISk, S, M,) inf. n. as above, (ISk, S,) He (a man, ISk, S) remained, stayed, dwelt, or abode, in the place. (ISk, S. M.) And رَيَّمَتِ السَّحَابَةُ فَأَغْضَنَتْ The cloud remained without clearing away [and rained continually]. (S, TA.) ―
-b3- And ريّم, inf. n. as above, He journeyed all the day. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
